paite: Thou sisa in gimlim bawlpa nuhtheihna uingim asawlkhesak a; huchi mah bang in haina neuchik in pilna leh zahna abukzou nak hi.
heading: Theihtelna A Kinga Paunakte
english: Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor; so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.

paite: Mipil lungtang ama khut taklam ah a-om a; himahleh mihai lungtang akhut veilam ah.
english: A wise man’s heart is at his right hand, but a fool’s heart at his left.

paite: Ahi, huai ban ah, lampi a mihai avak lai in, atheihsiamna in azuausan a, mi chiteng kiang ah hai ahihdan agen hi.
english: Yes also when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.

paite: Vaihawmmi lungsim nang dou ding a athohleh na mun taisan ke'n; kipiak in tatkhelhna thupite alungkimsak hi.
english: If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

paite: Gilou ni nuai a ka muh, vaihawmmi a kipan adiklouhna hong kipankhia bang in a-om hi.
english: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler.

paite: Haina nakpi a zahtakhuai in akibawl a, mun niam ah hauhsakna atu hi.
english: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place.

paite: Sikhate sakol tung a tuang leh lalte leitung a sikhate bang a khe a pai ka mu hi.
english: I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth.

paite: Kuapeuh kokhuk tou huai sung ah ake ding; kuapeuh dai phuvang; gulpi in akei ding.
english: He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.

paite: Kuapeuh suang hemkhia huai in akihih na ding a; kuapeuh sing a belh huai ah lauhuai in akibawl hi.
english: Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered by it.

paite: Sik amol a, mi'n ama atat-hiam keileh, hatna tamsem akoih ding ahi; himahleh pilna thuzoh aphatuam hi.
english: If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

paite: Khim a om ma a gulpi in akeihleh, khimmi ah phattuamna a-omta kei hi.
english: If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue.

paite: Mipil kam a thute hehpih thei in a-om a; himahleh mihai mukte'n amah mah anawmvalh ding.
english: The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips.

paite: Akam a thute kipatna haina ahi; huan ahoulimna tawpna lungsim kimlouhna gilou ahi.
english: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.

paite: Mihai in leng thu akhangsak a; himahleh mihing in bang a-om dia chih athei kei; huan amah nung a hong om ding, amah kua'n ahilh thei dia?
english: A fool also multiplies words. Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him?

paite: Khopi a hohna dan atheih louh ziak in, mihaite sepgimna in amaute lak a michih agimsak hi.
english: The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.

paite: Aw gam, na tung agik hi, na kumpipa naupang ahih lai in na lalte'n zingsang in ane uh!
english: Woe to you, land, when your king is a child, and your princes eat in the morning!

paite: Aw gam, na kumpipa miliante tapa ahih a, na lalte'n, kham ding hilou a, hatna ding a ahuntak a anek lai un, nuam na sa hi.
english: Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles, and your princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!

paite: Thadahna ziak in intung achim a; khut zawntatna ziak in inn akeh hi.
english: By slothfulness the roof sinks in; and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.

paite: Nuihna ding in ankuang a kilui a, uain in hinna akipaksak; sum thil tengteng awnghukna ahi.
english: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes the life glad; and money is the answer for all things.

paite: Kumpipa, na ngaihtuahna in hamsiat ke'n, na lupna dantan sung ah mihausate hamsiat ke'n; huihkhua a vasate'n na aw pua a, kha neite'n athu agen ding ziak un.
english: Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts; and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom, for a bird of the sky may carry your voice, and that which has wings may tell the matter.
